memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot." - Lev 14:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Ear, thumb, toe. If that sounds familiar, it is because these are the very places where blood was applied when Aaron and his sons were ordained as priests (Lev 8:23-24).

Think about what that means for the person standing there. The one who had been outside, shouting "unclean," is now being marked in exactly the same way as a priest of Israel.

And the three places speak for themselves. The ear — what I listen to. The hand — what I do. The foot — where I go. Hearing, working, walking. Between them they cover a whole life.

This is what redemption looks like. God does not merely wipe the slate and leave us to ourselves. He claims us — our attention, our labour, our direction — all of it under the blood.

Peter takes exactly this language and applies it to ordinary believers: you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood (1 Pet 2:9). Not just the leaders. Not just the impressive ones. You.

So ask the three questions today. What is my ear tuned to? What are my hands doing? Where are my feet carrying me? Christ's blood has claimed every one of them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has your ear been listening to most this week?
2. What are your hands doing that honours or dishonours God?
3. Where are your feet taking you that you need to reconsider?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You have claimed all of me — my hearing, my working, my going. Set apart my ears, my hands and my feet for Your service today. Amen.
